concept.name: CDN & Edge Caching

relationships.description: CDNs terminate client TCP/TLS connections physically close to users via Anycast to eliminate round-trip latency.
A CDN is essentially a globally distributed edge reverse proxy fleet with caching and DDoS mitigation.
Complements in-memory database caching (Redis) by filtering traffic before it reaches origin servers.

concept.tagline: Terminating TLS and caching content at Anycast edge PoPs via s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate, and Origin Shielding.

spark.summary: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) terminates TCP/TLS and serves cached responses from Anycast edge PoPs milliseconds from the user, collapsing cross-continental RTTs and shielding origin servers from 80-99% of read traffic.
spark.keyTakeaway: Edge caching is won or lost in HTTP cache headers and collapse controls: combine s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate, Origin Shielding, and request collapsing so edge misses never stampede your origin.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **Content Delivery Network (CDN)** is a globally distributed reverse-proxy tier that terminates TCP/QUIC and TLS at Points of Presence (PoPs) 5–20 ms from end users.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts User (Anycast) -> Edge PoP -> Origin Shield -> Authenticated Origin (Edge PoP (BLR) -> Origin Shield PoP -> Origin ALB (mTLS) -> App / S3 Origin); Anycast QUIC Handshake -> Key Normalization -> SWR Background Refresh (User (Bengaluru) -> Edge PoP (BLR) -> Origin Shield -> Origin Server); Merchant DB Update -> CDC Purge Worker -> CDN Surrogate-Key Eviction (Catalog DB Update -> CDC Purge Worker -> CDN Purge API -> Origin Shield).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Combine edge caching for network RTT reduction with Redis for personalized or fine-grained dynamic fragments. Global storefronts emit `Surrogate-Key` tags on catalog responses.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore HTTP caching semantics, cache stampedes, and TLS/DNS edge optimization.

learningJourney.title: What is CDN Edge Caching
learningJourney.explanation:
A **Content Delivery Network (CDN)** is a globally distributed reverse-proxy tier that terminates TCP/QUIC and TLS at Points of Presence (PoPs) 5–20 ms from end users.

Using **BGP Anycast**, every PoP announces the same IP prefix so routers send each user to the topologically closest healthy PoP. Inside HTTP headers, `max-age` controls the **browser** cache while `s-maxage` controls the **shared CDN** cache—letting you cache aggressively at the edge (e.g., 24h) with instant surrogate-key purging while keeping browser TTLs short (60s).

sectionDiagram.title: User (Anycast) -> Edge PoP -> Origin Shield -> Authenticated Origin

cards.label: Origin Shielding
cards.detail: Funneling 200 global PoPs through 1 regional Shield PoP collapses global cache misses into 1 origin fetch.

cards.label: Stale-While-Revalidate
cards.detail: Serves expired content in 0 ms while refreshing asynchronously in the background.

cards.label: Authenticated Origin Pull
cards.detail: Origin ALB verifies the CDN's client mTLS cert to close direct-to-IP DDoS bypasses.

sectionDiagram.summary: Anycast PoPs + Origin Shielding + mTLS Origin Pulls deliver 5-20 ms global reads while protecting origin capacity.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Key Normalization & Collapse Controls (and cache-busting traps)
learningJourney.explanation:
Misconfigured CDNs silently drop from 99% hit rate to 0% and DDoS your own origin:

1. **Query-String Cache Busting**: Marketing links append unique `?fbclid=xyz` or `?utm_source=ig` parameters, creating millions of distinct cache keys for the exact same page.
2. **Cookie Poisoning**: An analytics script sets a session cookie on the root domain, and default CDN rules bypass caching whenever a `Cookie` header is present.
3. **Vary-Header Explosion**: Returning `Vary: User-Agent` fragments the cache across thousands of browser strings instead of normalizing to `mobile`/`desktop`.

sectionDiagram.summary: Key normalization preserves hit rates, while stale-while-revalidate hides revalidation latency from users.

learningJourney.explanation: Combine edge caching for network RTT reduction with Redis for personalized or fine-grained dynamic fragments.

benefits: 5-20 ms RTT globally, HTTP/3 0-RTT, DDoS/WAF absorption before origin.
costs: Coarser invalidation than in-app Redis; requires careful header/cookie discipline.

benefits: Fine-grained per-user or per-object caching and complex assembly.
costs: Users still pay full cross-continental WAN RTT to reach the origin region.

benefits: Runs auth/A-B routing or HTML personalization at the PoP without hitting origin.
costs: Strict CPU/memory limits and eventual consistency for global KV stores.

knowledgeCheck.question: After a marketing campaign launches with `?fbclid=...` tracking parameters, your CDN cache hit rate drops from 96% to 4% and your origin database overloads. What is the fastest fix?

options.text: Normalize the CDN cache key to strip marketing query parameters (fbclid, utm_*) and enable Origin Shielding
options.feedback: Correct: unique tracking query strings create a distinct cache key per click unless stripped from the CDN cache key.

options.text: Set Cache-Control: private on all catalog pages
options.feedback: Setting private disables shared CDN caching completely, sending 100% of traffic to the origin.

options.text: Add Vary: User-Agent to every response
options.feedback: Vary: User-Agent fragments the cache even further.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
